Title: February 12, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting

Topic1.Title: Area 3 Planning Reserve Community Needs Assessment (Service Area Expansion Step Two)
Topic1.Summary: Staff presented the step two community needs assessment for the Area 3 Planning Reserve, identifying six needs including housing, fire storage, aging-in-place facilities, parkland, agriculture, and renewable energy. Council asked detailed questions about middle-income housing gaps, parkland standards, water, infrastructure costs, and staff capacity. Public speakers largely urged moving forward, while some opposed due to water, traffic, and habitat concerns. Council voted 7-2 to find the identified needs of sufficient priority to warrant further consideration of a service area expansion plan, and gave staff direction to bring back a guiding resolution on consent.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda and Agenda Amendment
Topic2.Summary: Council unanimously amended the agenda to remove item 6A and then unanimously approved the consent agenda items 2A and 2B.

Topic3.Title: Community Change Requests Reconsideration Following County Commissioners Action
Topic3.Summary: Staff reviewed five community change requests the Boulder County commissioners wanted reconsidered, including three land use requests near Gunbarrel and two comprehensive plan policies on area 2 annexation. Staff recommended against reconsideration, and council expressed no interest in reconsidering any of them.

Topic4.Title: Municipal Court Update
Topic4.Summary: Presiding Judge Jeff Khan and Court Administrator Devon Kiss Kelly reviewed 2025 case filings, which included rising traffic and photo enforcement, a jump in criminal cases, and increased quality-of-life citations near CU. They highlighted the community court, mental health counseling, parking appeals, and a new data dashboard. They also flagged Colorado Supreme Court's Camp decision and pending public defender legislation as legal changes to monitor.

Topic5.Title: Council Community Engagement Options for 2026
Topic5.Summary: Staff presented a menu of council engagement methods including chats with council, council-initiated chats, office hours, community connectors updates, and community and council forums. Council members expressed support for chats and forums, nominated a downtown bicycle security walk, and asked staff to return with estimated capacity for each method. The council engagement committee will refine the plan.
